# Startup readback: AI-41

## Confirmed control redesign amendment · 29 October 2026

The existing paired identity remains unchanged. The worker now has four externally visible states: active (heartbeat plus polling), online (heartbeat only/paused), offline (stopped or heartbeat expired), and revoked (stored for audit but hidden). Browser commands set a monotonic desired-state generation; heartbeat applies and acknowledges it before work, while poll is permitted only for active devices. Start is a clipboard-only launcher action and its command is never rendered in the page. The protocol lane owns the desired-state migration, authenticated control RPC, heartbeat/poll contracts and Windows runtime; UI and scan-history lanes consume these existing contracts. Focused proofs cover migration mapping, generation acknowledgement, paused heartbeat-only mode, resume without re-pairing, stop acknowledgement and active-only polling. Existing integration rules DB-03, DB-13, ACC-02, OPS-01 and WORKER-01 remain applicable; no new integration defect has been confirmed in this lane.

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

Harden the existing Windows worker device lifecycle and outbound task protocol, preserving its local-only role. Outcomes: (1) pairing, poll, heartbeat, result submission and revocation remain bound to a registered device and cannot be reused or replayed by another device; (2) claims, leases and revoked-device work follow the existing queue recovery contract; (3) the supported worker version/capabilities and device health are observable while the worker exposes no inbound listener and executes only its bounded signed action catalogue.

Existing contracts: authenticated-user JWT + fresh AAL2 MFA gate for site registration/revocation; per-device secret and Ed25519 public identity for outbound Edge calls; device-bound queue/lease ownership, audit/correlation and recovery. Using existing `worker-pair`, `worker-poll`, `worker-heartbeat`, `worker-submit-result`, `device-register`, `device-revoke`, shared `worker-auth`, and Windows worker client contracts; integration rules: DB-03, DB-13, ACC-02, OPS-01 and WORKER-01.

## Implementation and boundaries

The confirmed gap was protocol compatibility: the client did not send capability metadata, its advertised version diverged from package metadata, and poll did not reject unsupported workers before queue work. The shared Edge validator now requires the supported minimum version and inventory capability, rejects unknown capabilities before polling, and only offers signed actions when advertised. Heartbeat persists compatibility in the existing heartbeat status so the device UI can show upgrade/block reasons and capabilities. No migration was needed. Private keys remain device-bound, transport outbound HTTPS only, and action execution stays limited to typed signed manifests; no listener, arbitrary remote command execution, or auth/RLS/MFA changes were introduced.

## Corrective pass · 29 October 2026

Operator staging found the idle worker slept through its five-minute poll interval, exceeding the two-minute UI heartbeat freshness window. The runtime now caps sleep by the next heartbeat deadline (WORKER-09 / AI41-29). The same pass simplifies Devices and Digital Estate cards to title, colour-coded state, heartbeat and controls; removes the standalone start card and worker diagnostics; separates Launch Scan from Scan History; and capitalises scan labels/statuses. Focused worker cadence and display-state regressions are included; hosted proof remains the existing paired-worker manual sequence.
